objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Over the last three months I’ve been gradually finding it harder to walk, and in the past month I’ve needed a wheelchair. About a year ago I started having urinary incontinence, and more recently my speech has become slurred, with stiffness in my limbs and some tremor in my hands.”
[ASK] Have you experienced involuntary muscle jerks or abnormal movements (e.g., chorea) that are not typical of Parkinsonism?

“Not really—no jerks or abnormal flailing movements like chorea that I can recall, it’s mainly stiffness/rigidity and a hand tremor. I haven’t noticed any other unusual involuntary movements beyond that.”
[ASK] Does the patient have **autonomic dysfunction** (e.g., severe orthostatic hypotension, urinary retention/incontinence, or marked constipation)?

“Yes—I've had urinary incontinence for about a year, and I also get lightheaded with standing consistent with orthostatic symptoms.” “I wouldn’t say I have severe constipation, but I do have trouble controlling my bladder.”
